newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission reserves view on French maize threat.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission reserves view on French maize threat.

text.p: A threat by France to delay approval of genetically modified maize could lead to a new trans-Atlantic trade dispute, U.S. diplomats said on Friday.
"This is potentially serious but we are taking the view that there will be no problem once the proper notification has been sent to Paris," one diplomat said.
The European Commission expressed surprise at a threat by France to delay giving approval for putting genetically modified maize on the EU market because of a legal technicality.

France has said it will not give its approval until new EU labelling rules have been introduced. Officially France says it has not been given formal notice of the Commission's decision to approve genetically modified maize announced on December 19.

"We are surprised but not yet alarmed. We must wait to see what happens once the proper notification of the Commission's decision in December has been sent to Paris," spokesman Peter Jorgensen told Reuters.
French customs officials this week seized cargoes of modified maize and corngluten feed believed to contain modified maize.
Privately U.S. officials say that if France continues to block imports of modified maize "it will be raised at a very high level in Washington".
"We met with French officials in Paris this week and were assured by them that the delay is purely due to the lack of an official notification," one diplomat said.
